subject.name: Indian and western political thought
subject.course_or_branch: BA in Socialogy Psychology Political Science

content: Kautilya’s Arthashastra and the role of the king, Dharma as
governance., Plato’s ideal state and philosopher-king
Aristotle’s
politics and the concept of justice., Concepts of justice, statecraft
and the ruler's role in ensuring order in both Indian and Greek
traditions
Manusmriti’s vision of governance, Bhakti traditions and ethical
governance., Machiavelli’s pragmatic power politics, Hobbes’ social
contract and fear-based order., Realism and morality-contrasting
the Indian emphasis on Dharma and the Western focus on
pragmatism and authority

chapters.chapter_name: Liberalism, Reform, and the Social Contract
content: Raja Ram Mohan Roy and Brahmo Samaj’s reform movements
Dayanand Saraswati’s Vedic revivalism
Bentham and Mill’s
utilitarianism, anarchism and its critique of authority, Locke’s
theory of liberal government, Rousseau’s general will
Montesquieu’s separation of powers., Indian social reformers and
Western Enlightenment thinkers on rights, governance, and
reform-how both addressed social inequalities and political power
Gandhi’s non-violence and satyagraha, Ambedkar’s critique of caste
and Dalit rights, Nehru’s secular nationalism, Savarkar’s Hindutva
Marx’s critique of capitalism and class struggle, Indian and Western
critiques of authority, class, and identity-contrasting responses to
colonialism, industrialization, and modernization

chapters.chapter_name: Contemporary Critiques of Power and Justice
content: Subaltern studies and postcolonial critiques (Ranajit Guha), Dalit
feminism, modern debates on secularism., Foucault’s power and
discipline, Derrida’s deconstruction, Rawls’ theory of justice, and
Frankfurt School’s critical theory., Global South and North
perspectives on power, identity, and justice
